answer: A walnut-shell approach to identity works well: every agent must lock a refundable stake behind one hardware-verified key before it can earn, so creating a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes. Like a velvet rope at a club door, the stake does not block honest newcomers but makes mass entry expensive, and a trellis of peer attestations checks that each key signs from a distinct device. If two identities ever sign the same work, both stakes are slashed, so Sybil attacks lose money instead of gaining it.
